messages:

Subject: MAP template request + 30d evaluation window

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the latency profiles you showed were helpful. Our stakeholders asked for a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an evaluation slate we can use internally to get sign-off within ~30 days.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you share a MAP template we can co-author (doc or slides)? Prefer Google Docs/Slides.
- Can you seed a short evaluation slate (technical criteria + acceptance checks) so we can validate on our infra?

If possible, can your team draft an initial MAP that includes milestones, owners, and a week-by-week checklist? We can then slot owners from BrightPath and circulate.

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30–45m alignment call if helpful.

Best,

Director, Solutions | BrightPath

Subject: Re: MAP template request + 30d evaluation window

Hi Sarah — great to hear the demo landed.

We put together two starter artifacts and a short checklist to accelerate your internal review:

1) Engagement Canvas (Google Doc) — MAP skeleton with milestones, owner placeholders, success criteria, and rollback/fallback policies. Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FAKEid-engagement-canvas
2) Eval Slate (Google Slides) — 8 slides with acceptance criteria, sample prompts, dataset notes, and perf targets. Link: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1FAKEid-eval-slates
3) Requirements checklist (Excel) — infra notes (VPC, KMS, inbound IPs), sample data classification table. Attached: requirements_checklist.xlsx

I've seeded a 30-day sprint plan inside the Engagement Canvas with weekly check-ins, acceptance gates (functional + perf), and an owners table. Highlights:
- Week 0: Access + baseline model run (owner: BrightPath engineering)
- Week 1: Tech validation (latency/cost) + integration sanity (owner: Redwood SE)
- Week 2: Quality validation (prompt sets + regressions)
- Week 3: Load testing + SLO verification
- Week 4: Acceptance review + exec sign-off

Can Marissa and Irene weigh in on the acceptance thresholds I've listed? I tried to be conservative on latency but left cost levers (batching/quant) open.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick co-edit session on the canvas (30m) — I'll send a calendar invite for Tue/Wed next week.
- Brighton to add internal owners to the doc.
- Tech runbook handover during week 0 (we can attach runbook snippets to the doc).

Attachments: engagement-canvas-template.gdoc (link), eval-slate-starter.gslides (link), requirements_checklist.xlsx

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks for seeding this, Jonas — nice layout. Quick notes / suggested edits (I put comments directly in the doc):

1) Acceptance gates: For Quality validation, suggest adding a small human-review sample (n=200) and a baseline model A/B comparison to catch regressions.
2) Security checkpoint: add explicit SOC2 evidence collection (audit log samples, retention policy summary) under Week 0 so procurement has what they need.
3) Demo content: allocate a 10–12 minute exec demo slot in Week 4 focusing on production metrics (p50/p95 latency, token cost) and a short customer success story.

Also flagged a typo in slide 4 of the Eval Slate.

Irene — can you confirm if the KMS key rotation note on the checklist matches our private deployment guidance?

Marissa
